title: Progressive model activation with manifest-delta migration and tokenizer side-channel
creator: Maya Lin
description: Goal: Reduce model bootstrap tail latency and simplify the ingest pipeline by introducing a manifest-delta based migration path and a tokenizer side-channel for metadata negotiation. This ticket implements a progressive activation flow: a canonical lightweight loader will register a model manifest, apply delta updates for large shard maps, and perform staged weight activation while the tokenizer handshake happens over a small side-channel to avoid blocking bulk weight transport. Deliverables include loader facade code, manifest-delta writer/reader, side-channel protocol spec, integration tests, and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical loader accepts current weight formats and produces a normalized manifest within 2 minutes for 100GB model on test harness
Cold-start 95th-percentile token-gen latency reduced by >=20% in canary compared to master
Tokenizer negotiation moved to side-channel and no longer blocks shard download during progressive activation
All existing checkpoint formats still supported with unit tests covering format detection
Deployment plan and rollback steps documented in the linked runbook
tasks: Design side-channel protocol and message contract (schema + versioning)
Implement manifest-delta writer that emits small diffs for shard map and checksum updates
Create canonical loader facade that normalizes format metadata and exposes progressive activation API
Add adapter layer for legacy checkpoint formats to the canonical manifest producer
Integrate tokenizer side-channel into loader handshake and add non-blocking tokenizer init path
Add e2e integration tests (simulated slow network and partial shard availability)
Benchmark cold-start and steady-state under QA harness, produce perf report
Prepare canary rollout config and feature flag gating in runtime
Write migration runbook and rollback procedures
updates: 2025-02-13: Initial spike completed. Verified manifest-delta approach reduces manifest serialization size by ~60% for sharded checkpoints using synthetic dataset.
2025-02-18: Decision: use protobuf for side-channel messages to allow forward/backward compatibility; trade-off accepted (slightly larger binary vs schema clarity).
2025-02-21: PR #1423 opened for canonical loader facade (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423). Early review notes: ensure adapter API is async and cancellation-safe.
2025-02-26: Integration test harness added to CI and flakiness threshold set. Observed cold-start 95p improvement ~28% locally with progressive activation on 4-shard model.

2025-03-02: Blocker: legacy weight extractor relies on synchronous file manifests (ENG-71234). Short-term mitigation: adapter shim performs synchronous read then upgrades to async path; long-term follow-up scheduled.
2025-03-04: Tokenizer team reviewed side-channel draft and requested version field and explicit replay-tolerance semantics; awaiting final spec update before canary.
decision_history: Choose delta manifests vs full re-upload to reduce control-plane bandwidth and speed updates
Use protobuf over JSON for side-channel for schema evolution and binary compactness
Progressive activation default off behind feature flag; will enable for dedicated and private customers first
risks: Tokenizer side-channel mismatch could cause silent tokenization differences if versioning not enforced
Partial activation increases complexity of error handling when downloads fail mid-activation
Legacy adapters may introduce blocking IO on hot paths if not fully refactored
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest-delta roundtrip and backward compatibility
Simulated network partition tests with partial shard availability
Performance benchmark comparing master vs feature flag enabled across model sizes (10GB/50GB/200GB)
Canary deployment to internal staging cluster with traffic shadowing for 72 hours
